summary: Amertech Engineering is a small, long-established civil/environmental engineering, planning and surveying firm at 757 Ridgewood Avenue in North Brunswick, NJ, doing land-development site engineering and permit processing for private developers plus municipal engineering and board-review work for central New Jersey towns. Its front door is a phone number, a fax number and a circa-2000s table-based contact form on a Trellix Site Builder website last updated in 2016, with no hours, no online quote or booking, and no working click-to-call or email link. Work is visibly active (2025 subdivision and site-plan filings) and it was recruiting civil engineers in 2026, so intake, proposal and municipal-report coordination is handled by a small staff.

facts.fact: Services are land planning (feasibility studies, zoning analysis, concept plans, expert testimony) and site engineering (subdivision, roadway, grading and drainage, stormwater management, sanitary and water systems, sediment and erosion control, permits processing).

The firm states it and its predecessor firms have provided engineering services in New Jersey for over 80 years, and lists municipal service including Monroe Township (35 years), Plainsboro (19 years), Cranbury (10 years) and Clark (over 10 years), plus Boards of Education and Utility Authorities.

Contact page gives 757 Ridgewood Avenue, North Brunswick NJ 08902, phone 732.828.3535 and fax 732.249.0859, and asks visitors to complete a form with first/last name, email, company, mailing address, product/service and best way to contact.

The site is a legacy Trellix Site Builder page set (meta generator 'Trellix Site Builder'), with no viewport meta tag, the header email link hard-coded to mailto:ourname@ouraddress.com, an '© 2011 – 2016' footer, and a '757 Ridgewod Avenue' typo in the header.
Site navigation has only Home, About Us, Services, Client Profile, Project Profile and Contact Us — there is no careers, team, or staff page.

Client Profile lists private clients including Lennar, Pulte, Centex Homes, Matrix Development, Home Depot, Costco Wholesale, Magyar Saving Bank and Hotel Investors, alongside government and education columns.

Project Profile lists residential subdivisions from 69 to 947 units (e.g. Lennar 947-unit adult community in Monroe), hospital and medical-center site planning, warehouse projects at NJ Turnpike Exit 8A, and school-board and church/temple site plans.

Two full-time North Brunswick postings appeared for the firm — Professional Civil Engineer and Civil Engineer – Entry Level — both listed as closed about four months before this review; the engineer jobs board shows no open Amertech positions.
The company's 401(k) profit-sharing plan's most recent public Form 5500 filing (EIN 22-1834296, North Brunswick NJ) reports 26 participants and about $3.6M in plan assets.

Public property record for 757 Ridgewood Avenue: commercial parcel, building description 'AMERTECH OFFICE', built 1962, 3,400 sq ft interior space on 0.374 acres, zoned II in North Brunswick Township.

A July 16, 2025 preliminary plat for a major subdivision in Old Bridge Township ('Brookside Estates') was prepared by Amertech Engineering, Inc. and signed 'For the Firm' by Sharif H. Aly, Professional Engineer NJ Lic. No. 34669.
robots.txt on the site resolves to an empty file (zero bytes).

operations_signals: No online booking, quote request or client portal anywhere on the site; the only enquiry path offered is phone, fax, or the legacy web form (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)

Contact form is a table of plain fields (name, email, company, mailing address, product/service, best way to contact) with no project-type, parcel, municipality, deadline or file-upload fields, and no acknowledgement or ticket ID (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)
No office hours published on the site or on the contact page, so a caller cannot tell when the office is staffed (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)
Phone number appears as plain text with no tel: link and no click-to-call on the phone layout (https://amertechengineering.com/)
Header email link is broken — it points to a placeholder address instead of main@amertechengineering.com, so emailed enquiries from the site header go nowhere (https://amertechengineering.com/)

Firm works as municipal engineer/board reviewer and as private-consultant designer, i.e. two different intake rhythms: recurring municipal agendas and deadlines plus one-off developer scoping (https://amertechengineering.com/id1.html)
Expert testimony and permits processing are listed as services, implying scheduling of board appearances and application tracking handled by office staff (https://amertechengineering.com/id4.html)
hiring_signals: Professional Civil Engineer posting (full time, on site, North Brunswick): manage land-development projects from planning through design and permitting, prepare proposals, lead engineers/technicians/administrative staff, attend client and board meetings; 5–8 years experience and NJ PE license; AutoCAD Civil; closed ~August 6, 2026 (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)
Civil Engineer – Entry Level posting (full time, on site, North Brunswick), AutoCAD / AutoCAD Civil 3D tagged, also closed in the same period (https://engineerjobs.io/jobs-in-north-brunswick-nj)

No posting found for receptionist, administrative assistant, billing/AR, dispatcher or marketing roles — hiring is concentrated in technical delivery staff (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)

PE-level posting explicitly includes leading administrative staff and preparing proposals, so proposal writing and staff coordination sit with a senior engineer rather than a dedicated business-development role (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)
review_themes: No customer reviews found on Yelp, BBB, Angie's or similar consumer sources in searches; this is a B2B/professional-services firm with essentially no public customer-review corpus (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Amertech+Engineering+North+Brunswick+NJ)

An earlier browser pass of the Google listing showed a 3.4-star rating, no visible review count, 'Claim this business' and 'Add hours' prompts and no photos; I could not re-load the Maps panel in this pass, so treat the rating as unverified (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Amertech+Engineering+North+Brunswick+NJ)

Employee-side feedback exists but is thin: an employer review site showed roughly 2.9/5 from two ratings; the page itself blocked automated access, so this comes from a search snippet only (https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Amertech-Engineering-EI_IE721049.11%2C31.htm)

Municipal and planning documents show the firm's plans being reviewed and revised through 2025 (site plans revised April and August 2025 for a Raritan Borough redevelopment application), i.e. review-comment response cycles are a routine part of its workflow (https://www.raritanboro.org/_Content/pdf/Lagrange-St-Traffic-Study.pdf)
tech_footprint: Website runs on Trellix Site Builder, a discontinued consumer site builder; pages are HTML 4.01 table layouts with id-numbered filenames (index.html, id1.html, id4.html, id61.html) (https://amertechengineering.com/)
No viewport meta tag, so the 390 px phone view renders as a shrunken desktop page; no responsive layout (https://amertechengineering.com/)
No JSON-LD or other structured data, no meta description, and the page title is only the company name (https://amertechengineering.com/)
No booking widget, chat widget, CRM form handler, analytics tag or payment/portal integration visible in the page source; the form is a bare legacy form (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)
robots.txt is present but empty, and there is no sitemap.xml (returns 404) (https://amertechengineering.com/robots.txt)
Design stack evidenced by hiring ads is AutoCAD / AutoCAD Civil 3D plus stormwater software; there is no client-facing project portal (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)
Content footprint is thin and undated: client and project lists are static text with no case studies, photos of work, or downloadable reports (https://amertechengineering.com/id62.html)
growth_signals: Active 2025 project work: a major-subdivision preliminary plat prepared for Old Bridge Township dated July 16, 2025 (https://files-backend.assets.thrillshare.com/documents/asset/uploaded_file/1690/Old_Bridge_Township/efb1aa61-7a66-4f28-81b2-85092620a9ba/CIS-dated-July-16%2C-2025.pdf?disposition=inline)

Raritan Borough redevelopment documents reference Amertech-prepared site plans dated 2024 and revised in April 2025, with exhibits revised August 2025 (https://www.raritanboro.org/_Content/pdf/Lagrange-St-Traffic-Study.pdf)

Recruiting for both a licensed PE project manager and an entry-level engineer in 2026 suggests capacity expansion or replacement in technical delivery (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)

Long-tenure municipal relationships (Monroe 35 years, Plainsboro 19, Cranbury 10, Clark 10+) indicate recurring, renewable review work rather than project-by-project churn (https://amertechengineering.com/id1.html)
No new office, acquisition, award or press coverage found for 2024–2026 in searches; the firm appears to operate from the single North Brunswick office (https://njparcels.com/property/1214/168.02/77)
physical_signals: Single office: 757 Ridgewood Avenue, North Brunswick NJ 08902 (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)
Building is a 3,400 sq ft commercial structure described in the property record as 'AMERTECH OFFICE', constructed 1962, on a 0.374-acre lot zoned II (https://njparcels.com/property/1214/168.02/77)

Plan sheets and surveys are prepared and sealed in-house ('Civil & Environmental Engineers * Planners * Surveyors' branding; plans signed for the firm by a licensed PE) (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)

Work is delivered at client and municipal board meetings plus field investigations, per the firm's own PE job description — i.e. staff time is split between office design work and outside meetings/site visits (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)

Payroll/retirement scale suggests roughly two dozen people: 26 participants in the company 401(k) plan per its latest public Form 5500 (https://www.fiduciarysignal.com/plan/221834296/amertech-engineering-inc)
Office address carries a 'Ridgewod Avenue' typo on the site header, while the footer spells it Ridgewood (https://amertechengineering.com/)
decision_maker: Unknown from the company's own site — no owner, principal or manager is named on any page. Public record: 2025 project filings prepared by the firm are signed 'For the Firm' by Sharif H. Aly, Professional Engineer, NJ Lic. No. 34669 (https://files-backend.assets.thrillshare.com/documents/asset/uploaded_file/1690/Old_Bridge_Township/efb1aa61-7a66-4f28-81b2-85092620a9ba/CIS-dated-July-16%2C-2025.pdf?disposition=inline); a state licensing report indexed in search results named Michael H. Saperstein as licensee in charge, but that PDF now returns 404 and could not be verified.

inferences.inference: Enquiries arriving through the website are likely mishandled or lost: the header email link is a placeholder and the form has no acknowledgement path.
inferences.reasoning: The mailto target in the site header is literally 'ourname@ouraddress.com' rather than the firm's main@ address shown in text, and the contact form has no confirmation, ticketing or autoresponder behaviour described anywhere on the site.

inferences.inference: The firm is probably phone-first and paper/fax-tolerant, so an agent that answers, qualifies and routes enquiries would change the front door rather than replace an existing digital funnel.
inferences.reasoning: The only published contact methods are a phone number, a fax number and a generic form; there is no booking, quote, portal, chat or CRM evidence in the page source.

inferences.inference: A large share of staff hours goes to municipal agenda cycles and review-comment responses, which is repetitive document work an agent could draft.
inferences.reasoning: The About page lists roughly ten municipal appointments plus Boards of Education and Utility Authorities, and public filings show routine plan revisions and review-response letters (Raritan, Old Bridge, Cranbury).

inferences.inference: Proposal and scoping work is a bottleneck at the principal level.
inferences.reasoning: The PE job ad makes 'preparing proposals' and leading administrative staff part of a licensed engineer's duties rather than a dedicated marketing or business-development role.

inferences.inference: Headcount is roughly 20–30, not the '8 employees' a data aggregator claims.
inferences.reasoning: The company's own 401(k) Form 5500 reports 26 participants, and the firm advertises both a 5–8 year PE and an entry-level engineer while serving ~10 municipalities; the aggregator figure contradicts both.

inferences.inference: The Google listing, if unclaimed as the earlier pass suggested, makes the firm nearly invisible for 'civil engineer North Brunswick' style searches despite 80 years of work.
inferences.reasoning: Website has no meta description, no structured data, no town/service keywords in the title, and no hours; the Maps panel reportedly prompts to claim the business and add hours.

data_gaps: No browser tools were available in this pass, so the Google Business Profile (rating, review count, claimed status, hours, photos) could not be re-verified; the 3.4 rating and 'Claim this business' prompt come from the earlier triage pass.
Google Maps, LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Manta, YellowPages and BizStanding all blocked automated access (403 / JS-only), so headcount, officer names and employee ratings could not be read at source.
The NJ PELS Certificate of Authorization report URL cited in search results now returns 404; the licensee-in-charge name is therefore unverified.
No customer reviews of any kind were found — no Yelp, BBB, Angi or Google review text was retrievable, so no customer-voice themes can be summarised.
No office hours, service-area statement, pricing, fee schedule or turnaround commitments are published anywhere on the site.
Job postings' full text and salary were not readable at source (Indeed blocked); only the job-board summary and closed dates were available.
The contact form was not submitted (prohibited), so response-time and acknowledgement behaviour are untested.
One aggregator (visualvisitor.com) lists an 'Owner: David Luk' and '8 employees', which conflicts with the firm's Form 5500 participant count and is treated as unreliable; not used.
